input.quote: 14.6 Insurance. Each Party shall procure and maintain insurance, including product liability insurance, with respect to its activities hereunder and under the Ancillary Agreements and which is consistent with normal business practices of companies similarly situated
input.rationale: Section 14.6 is the only insurance provision in the agreement. It obliges each Party to carry insurance "consistent with normal business practices" (product liability named) but states no monetary limits and no professional liability (E&O) or cyber/privacy coverage. It therefore fails the fallback position, which requires E&O of at least USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of at least USD 2,000,000 from the counterparty. We target the fallback and add only the two missing minimum limits for RevMed, leaving Sanofi's self-insurance right, the evidence-on-request mechanic and the cancellation-notice obligation untouched.

ops.text: Minimum Coverages. RevMed shall maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 and cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.6 sets no minimum limits, so we add RevMed's floor coverages at our fallback position: E&O of USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy of USD 2,000,000. Sanofi's self-insurance right and the existing evidence-on-request mechanic are unchanged.
proposal.summary: Add minimum E&O (USD 1M) and cyber (USD 2M) limits for RevMed.

mappings.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
